> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1e251073cbf8a62cddfd10cb1ff005ddaadc1839` — the merge of head `2c06d027e8eb501d1f6c053f45d1f4f1a15a0b8b` into base `e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1e251073cbf8a62cddfd10cb1ff005ddaadc1839 && git checkout 1e251073cbf8a62cddfd10cb1ff005ddaadc1839
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e 2c06d027e8eb501d1f6c053f45d1f4f1a15a0b8b && git checkout -B drift-repro e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e && git merge --no-ff 2c06d027e8eb501d1f6c053f45d1f4f1a15a0b8b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e86530088a137275d803db29cb7c3afbc0f9f10e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2c06d027e8eb501d1f6c053f45d1f4f1a15a0b8b`
Local-runs: none

Read-only, at 2026-10-11T04:10Z: card #22636 (body and all 15 comments, including ruling `6104584601` letter B and the prior ruling `5791822697` item 3 on #19527), PR #22762 (body, its 6-file list, the net diff from the merge base `e7e6544ab9` to the head, every quoted sentence verified with `git show` at the head), and the head's check-runs. The seat's own comments (`6104682119`, `6105130863`, `6105210415`) were read as claims and re-derived, not adopted. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The one accept-set change — a flow whose start `config.triggerType` is a `record-*` string and whose `config.objectName` is absent (or not a non-empty string) is no longer judged for unbound flow CEL roots by `objectstack validate` — right, and "opens" is true at runtime.** The diff adds exactly one `open(...)` call to `flowCelEntrances` (`flow-cel-root-scope.ts:395`–`:398`): `if (kind === 'record_change' && !triggerObject)`, where `kind` is `resolveFlowTriggerKind(flow)` (`packages/spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts`: `record_change` iff the start node's `config.triggerType` is a string starting `record-`) and `triggerObject` is `nameOf(config.objectName)` (a non-empty string, else `undefined`). Traced on the runtime at this head, none of it touched by the diff:
- `AutomationEngine.deriveTriggerBinding` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts:3673`) resolves the kind through the same resolver and, in its `record_change` arm, binds `object: typeof config.objectName === 'string' ? config.objectName : undefined`, so an absent or non-string `objectName` binds `object: undefined`.
- `RecordChangeTrigger.start` (`packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts:309`–`:314`) calls `this.engine.registerHook(hookEvent, handler, { object: binding.object, packageId })` for each mapped lifecycle event. The ObjectQL door `assertValidHookObject` returns at once on `object === undefined` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:2932`), and the dispatcher `triggerHooks` (`:4644`) admits the entry through `hookMatchesObject` (`:2819`), whose documented semantic is "an absent `object` admits everything (global)". The hook therefore fires on a write to any object, declared by the stack or not.
- `buildContext` (`record-change-trigger.ts:389`, `:402`, `:511`) reads `object = binding.object ?? ctx.object`, builds the row from `previous`, the input payload and the after-row, and returns `record: isolatedRecord` (and `params: isolatedRecord`), so the run is handed that row, and `seedRunVariables` flattens its keys beside `record` (as review `6095756455` measured).
The build door cannot know the keys of a row from an arbitrary object, so leaving the flow unjudged is the module's existing rule for a record whose keys are not in hand, applied to a second shape. The widening is confirmed on the code, not on the dev's say-so.

**2. The widening is exactly the `Clause-②:` line, no more.** The new branch sits inside the per-flow start-node loop and keys only on `kind === 'record_change' && !triggerObject`. An array-form `triggerType` resolves to no kind in the spec resolver (its one documented divergence from the engine), so it never reaches this reason; the engine routes that shape to the trigger only to refuse it at bind, and lint already reports `flow-trigger-unknown-event`. A `record-*` string with a declared `objectName` is judged as before (pinned); `objectName` with no `record-*` token resolves to no kind and is judged (pinned); a `record-*` token with an undeclared `objectName` was already open. One reach the line leaves implicit, right by the already-published rule: a flow this reason opens is a parent like any open parent, so its `subflow` and `map` children open through the pre-existing fixpoint (`:459`–`:470`, untouched); the 22565 note already publishes "a subflow or map parent that is itself such a flow" as a stand-down. Nothing else newly opens, and nothing newly closes.

**3. Nothing moves at the runtime publish door — right; S stands.** `validate-expressions.ts` changes comment lines only (`:2169`–`:2175`); the code `const runtimeGateWrite = options.runtimeWriteType !== undefined` and `objectWrite || runtimeGateWrite ? new Map() : flowCelEntrances(stack, fieldIndex)` is byte-unchanged, so `flowCelEntrances` (and the new reason) is never consulted on a runtime write, and `perWriteSnapshotEntrance()` (`:2253`) is still what the scope receives there. `perWriteSnapshotEntrance`'s body (`flow-cel-root-scope.ts:489`–`:495`) is byte-unchanged; only its docblock moved. `runtime-gate.ts`, `authoring-rules.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol`, `packages/spec` and `packages/services` are untouched (`git diff --stat` over them is empty). W is not built; `CONTEXT_STACK_KEYS` and `RuntimeStackContext` are as ruling `5791822697` item 3 left them.

**4. S re-worded; its code and pins unchanged — right.** The three `it` blocks of the S describe (the gate passes `user.id` on edge `e1` while the brace-trap verdict still refuses on `e2`; the build door refuses the same root on the same flow; the stand-down names the per-write snapshot) lie outside every diff hunk; only the describe title and two docblocks changed, plus the module section and the `perWriteSnapshotEntrance` docblock in `flow-cel-root-scope.ts` and the comment in `validate-expressions.ts`. The new wording cites ruling `5791822697` item 3, ruling `6104584601` and ADR-0109 Decision §3; that section's own text is about `skill.tools[]` resolution over the whole stack, and the citation follows both rulings' reading of it as "cross-item reference resolution belongs to the whole-stack rule", which is acceptable because both rulings cite it that way. No text anywhere still promises a widening: `git grep 22636` at the head over `packages content/docs skills docs .changeset` returns the two citations (`flow-cel-root-scope.ts:156`, the test at `:419`) plus two unrelated matches on comment-id digits in `plugin-security` and `plugin-sharing` tests; a sweep of `until|widen|yet|temporar|hold-out` over the lint files that carried S finds only the new "Not a hold-out awaiting a wider snapshot" sentences and unrelated history; `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` has no snapshot or stand-down wording for the flow CEL root judgment (its two "runtime publish gate" mentions, `rule-explanations.ts:1368` and `:1474`, belong to other rules); every other pending changeset's "Never at the runtime gate" line states what the snapshot carries and promises nothing.

**5. The owed `map`-child pin — a pin only, with a control — right.** The new `it` (test `:380`–`:397`) uses a `map` node whose `itemObject` is the declared `acct`, so the node cannot open `f` by itself; an `api`-typed parent `g` is open by its own trigger, and the pin asserts `f` draws no refusal and its `openedBy` matches `map node 'each' in flow 'g' … 'g' is itself open`; then two levels, `g → map → h → map → f`; then the red control: the same `map` node in a parent no entrance opens leaves `f` judged (one refusal). It exercises only the `map`-edge and fixpoint code (`:447`–`:470`), none of which is in the diff, so it was green before the fix by construction, as the dev reports; `map-node.ts` (about `:177`–`:186`) confirms what it pins: the child context spreads the parent's and sets `record` only for an id-bearing item. Carries `6096005997` and review `6095756455` ③.

**6. The record-trigger pin is a true pin of the change.** `flowStack({ edgeCondition: USER, triggerType: 'record-after-update' })` builds a start node with the token and no `objectName`; before the diff that flow was handed `record` but not opened, so `user.id` drew one refusal, and the `toEqual([])` assertion had to be red on the unfixed source, as the dev reports from the pins-first commit `49c47a4e51`. The controls (declared `objectName` → one refusal; no token → one refusal) and the direct `flowCelEntrances` read (`openedBy` names `'record-after-create'`, `bound` is `['record']`) match the reader at the head.

**7. Docs — no false shipped sentence.** The drift comment's 13 pages are listed through the generic `record_change` literal. None states the build door's unbound-root judgment or how `record` binds for an `objectName`-less record trigger: a grep for unbound-root, `Unknown variable`, `expression-invalid` with flow or CEL, and `current_user` with flow or CEL over `content/docs` hits only `flows.mdx:1812`–`:1813` (the CEL evaluation table, runtime semantics this PR leaves alone) and unrelated pages; `validating-metadata.mdx:704` describes the per-write snapshot without promising to widen it; every `objectName` in `flows.mdx` is CRUD-node or screen config. Nothing to correct.

**Check-runs on the head (the read above; 40 runs):** 31 success, 5 skipped (Auto Label and Check PR Size duplicates from the body-edit re-fire, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in), 2 failure (both `Check Changeset`, below), 2 in progress at review time: `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`. Green among the completed: Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test Core 1/6, 4/6, 5/6 and 6/6, Dogfood Regression Gate (three shards and the summary), Dogfood Verify CLI, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), TypeScript Type Check, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, and the four claim guards. No red other than the designed one.

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION — written confirmation (`check-empty-changeset`'s foreign-changeset rule, #17712).** `Check Changeset` is red on this head by design, in both runs (`114381709085`, `114382787294`): the failing step is step 12, "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR", which runs `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs --base` on the merge base and carries the #17712 rule; step 11 "Require a changeset" is green because the PR adds a note of its own; steps 13 (ADR-0087 disposition) and 15 (major guard) are green. The failure annotations name exactly `.changeset/22565-flow-cel-unbound-root-refused.md` and `.changeset/22677-flow-cel-record-entrance.md`, each with the gate's two-class text whose DELIBERATE CORRECTION remedy is "do NOT restore it -- say so on the PR and get it confirmed". `pr-automation.yml` at `origin/main` triggers on `pull_request` only (`types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled, edited]`; `merge_group` appears nowhere in the file), and its route 0 text says: a PR whose only `.changeset` rows are CHANGED, not added, corrects somebody else's pending note — do not apply `skip-changeset`, write the confirmation naming the note and what changed, leave the check red (#18375). Per `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/landing-operations.md` at `origin/main` (lines 15–16), a PASS record at this tier on the same head is that confirmation when it names each modified note and judges each rewritten sentence. Both notes, judged:

- **`.changeset/22565-flow-cel-unbound-root-refused.md`, line 34** (added by PR #22609; front matter `@objectstack/lint` major, `@objectstack/spec` major).
  Old, at the merge base `e7e6544ab9`: "- **The runtime publish gate:** a flow write there is not judged for unbound roots yet. Its per-write snapshot carries no actions or other flows, so it cannot see those entrances. Every other expression verdict at that door is unchanged."
  New, at the head: "- **The runtime publish gate:** a flow write there is not judged for unbound roots, by design (rulings `5791822697` item 3 and `6104584601`). Its per-write snapshot carries no actions or other flows, so it cannot see those entrances. Every other expression verdict at that door is unchanged."
  True. Ruling `6104584601` letter B rules the stand-down "by design, not a hold-out"; ruling `5791822697` item 3 is "No snapshot widening: `RuntimeStackContext` / `CONTEXT_STACK_KEYS` are unchanged"; the code at the head matches both (`validate-expressions.ts:2253` hands `perWriteSnapshotEntrance()` on every `runtimeWriteType` write; `CONTEXT_STACK_KEYS` is untouched). Only "yet" left and the two citations arrived; the clause about what the snapshot carries is still true. Nothing else moved: the front matter (lines 1–4) hashes equal at base and head (sha256 `89f8d6ef1fa2b07c…`); the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line and the adr-0087 "registered" marker are byte-identical (`c6a833275aef7d04…` at both); `git diff -U0` shows one hunk of one line.
- **`.changeset/22677-flow-cel-record-entrance.md`, line 20** (added by PR #22730; front matter `@objectstack/lint` major).
  Old, at the merge base: "**Not judged.** The stand-downs of the unbound-root rule are unchanged. At the runtime publish gate this judgment still stands down: its per-write snapshot carries no actions and no other flows, so it cannot see an entrance, and a flow write there is not refused for `record` until that snapshot carries them."
  New, at the head: "**Not judged.** The stand-downs of the unbound-root rule are unchanged. At the runtime publish gate this judgment still stands down: its per-write snapshot carries no actions and no other flows, so it cannot see an entrance, and a flow write there is not refused for `record`, by design (rulings `5791822697` item 3 and `6104584601`)."
  True, for the same two rulings and the same code; `record` is entrance-derived since #22677 and the S stand-down covers it (the `record` block's gate pin, unchanged). The untouched opening clause "the stand-downs … are unchanged" describes #22677's own change and stays true of it; this PR's added open reason is published by its own note. Nothing else moved: the front matter hashes equal (`ea0bb786c46b79eb…`); the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line and the adr-0087 "not-required" marker are byte-identical (`8d873874852a98c3…` at both); one hunk of one line.

Both notes are still PENDING: present on `origin/main` (`e86530088a13…`) with the same blobs as the merge base (`cbddb31a64`, `4d8e6b7078`); `packages/lint/CHANGELOG.md` on `origin/main` has no match for `flow-cel-unbound-root-refused|unbound roots|snapshot carries them|flow CEL expression that reads`, and `.changeset/pre/` holds neither. No other pending changeset promises the widening: `git grep -i -E "snapshot carries them|unbound roots yet|until #22636|22636 widen|widens? (that |the )?snapshot|stand-?down.{0,80}(yet|until|temporar)|(yet|until|temporar).{0,80}stand-?down"` over `.changeset` at the head returns 0 hits (2 at the previous head `337de825af`, the dev's control). Confirmed: leave the red standing, restore neither file, apply no `skip-changeset`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22636-flow-cel-record-trigger-no-object-opens.md`: `'@objectstack/lint': minor` — right. The diff publishes in one package (`packages/lint/src/**`), and what it publishes is an accept-set widening of `objectstack validate` (one fewer refused shape) with no interface change and no narrowing. `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s level axis (#16055) requires a PR declaring `Clause-②: yes` to grade at least one package whose `packages/**/src/**` it moves at `minor` or above; `major` would overstate a non-breaking widening and `patch` is what that axis refuses. The repo is in pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json`, tag `next`), which changes nothing here. The `Clause-②:` line is byte-identical in the claim `6104682119`, PR body line 2 and the changeset (sha256 of the line `07fe8e380f1d316f…` for all three): `Clause-②: yes (widening: a flow whose `record-*` trigger names no start `config.objectName` opens, so `validate` no longer reports an unbound flow CEL root there)`. The note's prose is true against the code (the no-filter hook, the row handed as `record` with its fields flattened beside it, the same treatment as a record trigger on an undeclared object, the trigger shape not refused, the gate's stand-down by design) and against the ruling. It carries no adr-0087 marker and needs none (`minor`, non-breaking; `Check Changeset` step 13 is green). PR body line 1 is `Fixes #22636`, as the ruling orders: this card carries the small PR and closes with it.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every flag in `6105118633` and `6105200615`, and the thread's open items:
- Round-0 deviation 1: the no-promise criterion failed over `.changeset/` — carried into patch round 1 by seat order `6105130863`; verified 0 hits at the head over `.changeset` (above), and the grep over `packages content/docs skills` finds only the two citations. Answered.
- Deviation 2: `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` carries no S wording — verified by grep; nothing is owed behind the seat's #22161 slice 8. Answered.
- Deviation 3: level `minor` — answered in ②.
- Deviation 4: the four commits carry the session-link trailer and a generic co-author trailer, and no model id — a process note with no accept-set bearing. Recorded.
- Deviations 5–6 (a lock re-queue, an extra build so `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` could measure, the re-run after `337de825af`): process notes; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts this record reads.
- Deviation 7: zero label writes, `skip-changeset` not applied — right, and required: route 0 forbids the label on a corrected foreign note, and the PR adds a changeset of its own.
- Patch-round deviation 1: `check-empty-changeset` red by design — confirmed in writing above.
- Patch-round deviation 2: the worktree was recreated — process note.
- `open_questions`: none in either report. The earlier `needs_decision` report's three questions (`6102874585`) were closed by ruling `6104584601` (Q1 → B; Q2 moot under B; Q3 → open the flow, do not refuse the shape). Its out-of-scope finding (`RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema.path`'s describe omits datasets, name-keyed since #19143) is assigned by the ruling to a separate spec card the seat files; not this PR's. Escalated to the seat as still owed unless already filed.
- The two items earlier reviews owed to this card — the `map`-child pin (`6096005997`, review `6095756455` ③) and the opened-set gap (`6102568544`, review `6102167316` ③) — both land here, verified in ① 1, 5 and 6.
- Reviewer's flag, not blocking: the one input on which lint's reading and the engine's diverge is `objectName: ''`. `nameOf('')` reads no name, so lint now opens the flow; the engine binds `object: ''` (it is a string), and `registerHook` refuses that at the door (`assertValidHookObject`: an empty allow face would register a global hook), so `activateFlowTrigger` records the flow as refused to arm and it never fires. For that one shape the open reason's sentence ("fires on a write to any object") is not true; the consequence is an unjudged flow that cannot run (a false pass, never a false refusal or a false message to the author), the `nameOf` convention predates this PR (the undeclared-object reason read `''` the same way), and no corpus trigger has it (20 of 20 name an object). Not a condition of this verdict. The gap it exposes is pre-existing and elsewhere: a record trigger with a blank `objectName` passes `validate` (trigger-readiness judges only a named, undeclared object) while the runtime refuses to arm it — an ADR-0078 silently-inert declaration. Escalated to the seat as a trigger-readiness card candidate.
- Reviewer's note: a flow this reason opens also opens its `subflow` and `map` children through the fixpoint (① 2). Within the published rule; the `Clause-②:` line names the flow, which is the shape authors write.
- The diff touches no `packages/spec/src/**` path; this review is owed by the declaration limb (`Clause-②: yes`) alone, which the ruling names.

`Check Changeset` is red on `2c06d027e8` by design. It stays red, and this PR enters the queue with it, for these reasons:
